outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, is there observable progress toward putting the paper into the cup—for example, the paper visibly entering or crossing the cup opening—rather than merely being nearby or held in front of it?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the edited image visibly shows the paper entering the identifiable cup or otherwise progressing into its opening. Fail when the relevant objects and their placement are clear and the paper is merely nearby, held in front of the cup, or on its rim, with no insertion progress. Unknown when the cup, paper, opening, or their spatial relation cannot be reliably identified or resolved.
nodes.binding: Assess the requested paper-into-cup edit using visible source and edited image evidence. Do not infer insertion from proximity, contact, or a hand holding the paper near an object; do not treat an unidentifiable object as the cup.

nodes.question: Is the paper visibly inside the identifiable cup and visibly stuffed into it, rather than merely entering, resting on the rim, or being held nearby?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the edited image clearly shows the paper inside the cup and visibly pushed or compressed into it, not merely crossing the opening or resting loosely on the rim. Fail if the cup and paper are identifiable and the image clearly shows the paper is not inside and stuffed into the cup. Unknown if object identity, the cup interior, or the paper’s placement/action cannot be resolved.
nodes.binding: Use the image evidence to assess completed stuffing, distinct from the progress proposition in s1. A pass requires visible interior placement and evidence of being pushed or compressed into the cup; do not infer this from proximity or from s1 alone.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Interpret s1 as evidence of progress only and s2 as evidence of completed stuffing. Report complete only on s2 pass. Report partial only when s1 passes and s2 establishes that completion has not occurred; proximity alone is not progress. Report absent only when s1 clearly fails with relevant objects and placement resolved. If necessary evidence is unknown or the supports do not establish a faithful composition, report unknown. Do not count dependent observations as independent confirmation.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
